reviews.comment: I had Dr. Wendt a few years ago and he has had one of the longest impressions for me. His lectures were amazing and I have never had someone so passionate to teach. You must go to class and take notes the entire time (so don't take as an 8 am). Tests pull directly from his lectures. He is super nice and proofread my essay before turning it in.

Crucial piece of this class is showing up and taking notes. 90% of what is on the exam is what he goes over in class. I never read a chapter of the book, just studied the quizzes thoroughly and the notes I took, the night before the exam. Give some effort and show him you care, and you'll be fine.

John Wendt makes super interesting lectures that are engaging if you engage with them with questions. The only thing that will stop you from getting a high grade is if you don't do the online quizzes and not going to class. This is a very lecture heavy course and your grade in the class will reflect your attendance.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is awful, his lectures are very boring and he isn't loud enough to be heard clearly most of the time. He wants his class averages to be very low and doesn't give many opportunities to improve your grade. I dread this class and hate that his lectures are solely verbatim with no information on the slides. If you can, take ANYONE else.

The class isn't easy but as long as you read the chapter summaries from the textbook, study your notes, and show up for every class, you will do well. There wasn't a lot of homework which was nice. Just a weekly reading and textbook quiz with unlimited attempts. He has great lectures and cares about teaching. I would recommend (just don't skip!)

PLEASE read this. This is one of the worst profs i have ever had. The other reviews on here are teachers pets. I am telling you the truth when i saw he sets higher standards then should be in place for the class. I am very good at history but he said that a test average of 70 was "too high". Get an easier prof for the same class. Its worth it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed this class, especially for someone who generally doesnt typically enjoy history. The only thing I didnt like was having it at 5:45pm-7. Tests are very lecture heavy and all the quizzes come straight from the book so make sure you get the textbook. The powerpoint are uploaded online but he doesnt have any text on them.

Although attendance isn't mandatory, I would really recommend going to lectures because that is where most of the information comes from. He is a very intelligent professor and it is clear he is passionate about what he is teaching. There is quite a bit of reading, but if you space it out then it's not bad at all. I thoroughly enjoyed the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is not an easy A and he doesn't want it to be. The exam averages are in the high Cs and he wants them there. There are 3 exams, 1 essay, and weekly homework. The exams aren't cumulative but they will cover even the smallest details of the textbook/lecture. The lectures are long and dense, but he knows history well and he's a kind man.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you excel in history, this class should not be a problem. If you do not, good luck getting an A. His tests are too difficult for an introductory history class (doesnt want 100s), class is very lecture heavy and inconsistent some times, and lots of textbooks readings. He is however very passionate and assigns unlimited attempt quizzes weekly.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wendt is very passionate and amazing at what he does. His exams are very lecture heavy but just go to class and youll be fine. Honestly one of the best professors ive had. Weekly quizzes with unlimited attempts and one essay which isnt bad (i got a 100) so take him if you can! Very nice guy.

Quizzes, unlimited attempts--easy. but I worked my butt off for this class and i only got a B. He makes you work for it for only being a level 1 class. his exam questions are ones you need to read the textbook, youre not gonna know it by heart most likely if ur not into history like that. exams r mixed with lectures too. HE GRADES HARD on essay
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved his class! Super lecture heavy, but if you take good notes then you won't have to study a ton. One essay you have to write, but exams were non-cumulative and he never asks for a date or a specific name, very broad knowing but I learned a ton. You can tell he really loves history and wants his students to learn.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice and passionate professor. Lectures go over a lot of material and during every class it seems we're behind and have to cover excess material. Exams match the lectures so if you take solid notes you should be good. I'd definitely recommend him, but don't treat it like a blowoff class - averages on exams were in the 70's.

Wendt is an amazing professor! His lectures were so interesting and engaging and he makes grading criteria very clear for the students. He is also a very lenient professor and super accessible. If you can, TAKE HIM!! Super sweet guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Wendt is a great choice for Hist 105!! He is very understanding and considerate. As long as you go to lecture and take notes you will have no problem getting an A in this class. There are weekly quizzes with unlimited attempts so they are easy 5/5 to help your grade. 3 exams and 1 essay. No cumulative exam and they are all based on lectures
